pr_events.title: adt: fix inverted shrink check in vector pop_back, pop_front and erase
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Fixes #902. The shrink check in `vector_pop_back`, `vector_pop_front` and `vector_erase` was backwards, so I flipped it to match `vector_resize` and added two tests in `adt_vector_test` for it (capacity stays the same on a full vector, and only shrinks once size goes below capacity / 8).

Once the fix was in, `adt-trie-test` started failing under ASan with a use-after-free. The trie code was reading `vector_back` after `vector_pop_back`, which only worked before because pop never reallocated on small vectors. So the first commit copies the node out before popping. All tests pass locally with ASan.

pr_events.title: adt: return error in set_small_insert when the set is full
pr_events.body_excerpt: Fixes #904. `set_small_insert` now returns 1 when the key is new and the set is already full, instead of writing past the end. The check is after `set_small_find`, so overwriting a key that's already there still works on a full set (the existing test does that). Added an `InsertWhenFull` test in `adt_set_small_test`, it hits the heap-buffer-overflow under ASan without the fix. All tests pass locally with ASan.

pr_events.title: Fix silent truncation-without-termination in metacall_execution_path
pr_events.body_excerpt:
### Summary
Fixes a truncation silence bug in the `metacall_execution_path()` function of `metacall.c`, by taking the same approach that was applied to the `metacall_load_from_file_ex()` function before it.
### Long description

In `metacall_execution_path()`, the incoming path string was copied to a fixed `LOADER_PATH_SIZE` buffer by using `strncpy(path_impl, path, LOADER_PATH_SIZE - 1)` without checking the input length first, leading to possible silent truncation of a valid correctly null-terminated path that is longer than the `LOADER_PATH_SIZE - 1` bytes.

### Proposed changes
1. Regression test (`metacall_path_overflow_test.cpp`): the test `TEST_F(metacall_path_overflow_test, ExecutionPathOverflow)` passes a 5000-character long null-terminated string to `metacall_execution_path("mock", ...)`, and is expected to return a non-zero code, but currently fails on `develop` (returned 0).

2. Core fix (`metacall.c`): use `strnlen(path, LOADER_PATH_SIZE - 1)` to check the length,

pr_events.title: portability: keep null terminator inside buffer in get_fullname and get_directory
pr_events.body_excerpt: Fixes #907. `get_fullname` now stops copying one byte early so the `\0` always fits, and `get_directory` clamps `last` to `directory_size - 1` the same way `get_directory_inplace` already does. Both also return 0 for a zero sized buffer. Added two tests in `portability_path_test` that pass a buffer exactly as long as the result and check the byte right after it isn't touched, they fail without the fix. All tests pass locally with ASan.

pr_events.title: tests: allow running only some tests with memcheck
pr_events.body_excerpt:
As discussed with @viferga on Discord, first step for making the valgrind CI easier to work with. Right now `make memcheck` always runs every test and dumps all the logs at once, so you can't check just one test. This adds a `MEMCHECK_TEST` env var that gets passed to ctest as `--tests-regex`:

```sh
MEMCHECK_TEST=adt-vector-test make memcheck
MEMCHECK_TEST='adt-(set|map)' make memcheck
```

It also deletes the old `MemoryChecker.*.log` files before running, otherwise the logs from a previous full run would still get printed after a filtered one. Without the var it behaves the same as before. Added a short note in the docs too.

Tested locally with valgrind 3.26: full run still goes through all 37 tests, `adt-vector-test` alone runs one test and prints only its log, the regex one runs the 3 set/map tests, and a name that doesn't match just says no tests found.

pr_events.title: tests: make memcheck fail on valgrind errors and leaks
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Follow up to #909, as discussed with @viferga. Valgrind was exiting with the test's own exit code, so a test that leaks or does an invalid read still passed under `make memcheck`. This adds `--error-exitcode=1` so those tests get marked as failed by ctest (the python valgrind job already does the same).

"Still reachable" memory isn't counted as an error by valgrind, so it doesn't fail anything. Those are the `Defects: 1` you see on most metacall tests because of `--show-reachable=yes`, they stay as they are.

Tested locally with valgrind 3.26 on the core tests (mock loader only). The only one that fails now is `metacall-path-overflow-test`, which has 176 bytes definitely lost from `loader_impl_allocate` that we never saw before because it still passed. I'll look at that leak separately. `MEMCHECK_TEST=adt-vector-test make memcheck` still passes.

pr_events.title: loader: free handle and type maps of loaders that were never initialized
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Follow up to #910. With memcheck failing on leaks now, `metacall-path-overflow-test` was the only core test failing, with 176 bytes definitely lost from `loader_impl_allocate`.

The `ExecutionPathOverflow` test calls `metacall_execution_path("mock", ...)` without loading anything, so the mock loader gets created but never initialized. In `loader_impl_destroy` the loader's own destroy only runs when `init == 0`, and that's the one that ends up calling `loader_impl_destroy_objects` through `loader_unload_children`. So for a loader that was never initialized, `handle_impl_path_map`, `handle_impl_map`, `handle_impl_init_order` and `type_info_map` were never freed. Now it calls `loader_impl_destroy_objects` directly in that case. A loader that failed to initialize goes through the same path, so it's covered too.

Tested locally: `MEMCHECK_TEST=metacall-path-overflow-test make memcheck` goes from 176 bytes definitely lost to 0 errors, full `make memcheck` passes all 37 tests, and the ASa

pr_events.title: loaders/py_loader: fix asyncio shutdown deadlock and SIGPIPE crash (#803)
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Description
Problem
Shutdown Deadlock: The Python loader previously used threading.Thread to execute the background asyncio event loop. During runtime shutdown, the main thread attempted to join the Python thread while holding the GIL. The worker thread required the GIL to process the loop.stop() cleanup and terminate, causing a circular deadlock. Skipping the join prevented the hang but caused segmentation faults due to interpreter finalization running while the thread was still active.

Solution
Native OS Threading Abstraction (source/threading): Added a cross-platform C-level thread API (threading_thread.h) implemented via POSIX pthreads (threading_thread_unix.c) and Windows CRT _beginthreadex (threading_thread_win32.c).

C-Managed Event Loop: Migrated the background asyncio loop execution to run inside a native OS thread managed from C land.

Deadlock-Free Teardown: In py_loader_impl_finalize_asyncio_module, the GIL is released via Py_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS before invoking th

pr_events.title: metacall: validate argument count against METACALL_ARGS_SIZE before marshalling
pr_events.body_excerpt:
# Description

The public marshalling entry points in `metacall.c` gather arguments into a
fixed-size stack array:

    #define METACALL_ARGS_SIZE 0x10
    void *args[METACALL_ARGS_SIZE];

The loop bounds that fill that array come from the callee signature
(`signature_count`) or from a deserialized document, neither of which the C
caller controls. Nothing compared those counts against `METACALL_ARGS_SIZE`,
so a loaded function declaring more than 16 parameters wrote past the end of
the array.

This adds a `metacall_args_size_validate()` helper and calls it before any
write in every affected entry point. On failure the call returns `NULL` (or
`1` for `metacall_register`) and logs the count and the limit, so the caller
gets a clear error instead of a stack smash. The document-driven paths
(`metacallfs`, `metacallfms`, `metacallfs_await`, `metacallfms_await`) destroy
the deserialized value before returning so the early-out does not leak it.

pr_events.body_excerpt:
# Description

With guidance from @viferga, in `py_loader_impl_value_to_capi`, the `TYPE_MAP` branch converts each key and value
to a Python object and inserts them with `PyDict_SetItem`. `PyDict_SetItem` does not
steal references (unlike `PyList_SetItem` / `PyTuple_SET_ITEM` used in the other
branches), so the dict takes its own reference and ours were never released.
This leaked every key/value passed from MetaCall to Python as a dict.

pr_events.title: node_loader: free await trampoline after resolve and reject
pr_events.body_excerpt:
`node_loader_impl_func_await_safe` and `node_loader_impl_future_await_safe` allocate a `loader_impl_async_func_await_trampoline` and attach it to a JS object with `napi_wrap`, using `node_loader_impl_async_func_await_finalize` as the finalizer.

When the promise settles, `node_loader_trampoline_resolve` / `node_loader_trampoline_reject` call `napi_remove_wrap` on that object. Once the wrap is removed, node does not call the finalizer anymore, so the trampoline (48 bytes) leaked on every await.

The fix deletes the trampoline in resolve/reject after the callback runs. The callback context isn't owned by the trampoline, so it isn't touched.

### Valgrind (`MEMCHECK_TEST=node make memcheck`, debian bookworm, node 18.20.4)

Before, metacall-node-async-multiple-test:
```

pr_events.title: node_loader: free promise context when resolved in the js thread
pr_events.body_excerpt:
# Description

Found this one while going through `metacall-node-port-await-test` under valgrind.

When you call `metacall_await` from node, `node_loader_impl_promise_await` creates a promise context. If the promise gets resolved/rejected from the JS thread itself, `node_loader_impl_handle_promise` calls `node_loader_impl_handle_promise_safe` directly and the uv async handle never gets initialized. But `destroy()` only frees the context inside the close callback of that handle, and since the handle was never initialized, `close()` does nothing. So the context (184B) and the copied result (52B) leak on every await.

The fix: if the handle was never initialized, just free the context directly in `destroy()`. The cross-thread path stays the same.

On develop you don't see this as its own record because it's reachable from the await trampoline (#929), so these logs are with #929 applied.

pr_events.title: node_loader: destroy await future right after awaiting from the port
pr_events.body_excerpt:
# Description

This is the 88B that was left in `metacall-node-port-await-test` after #931.

When you call `metacall_await` from node, `node_loader_impl_promise_await` gets a future back from `metacall_await_s`. That future holds a ref to the inner promise (`napi_create_reference` in `node_loader_impl_napi_to_value`), and it was attached to the returned promise with `node_loader_impl_finalizer`, so it only got destroyed when that promise was collected. In practice that happens at teardown, and by then the loader is already marked as destroyed, so `future_node_interface_destroy` skips `napi_delete_reference` and the ref leaks.

The promise gets resolved/rejected through `handle_promise_safe`, not through the future, so nothing needs the future after `metacall_await_s` returns. The fix just destroys it right there instead of waiting for the finalizer. We're on the JS thread and the loader is alive at that point, so the ref gets deleted properly.

I also tried enabling the `< 18`

pr_events.title: feat: cache Rust dependencies in PR Check Build
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Closes #1619

### What

`pr-check-build.yml` recompiled the full Rust/Tauri dependency tree on every run. This PR caches it so only the `picto_py` crate rebuilds.

- **Rust cache:** `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` on `frontend/src-tauri/target`, keyed on `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml` and the rustc version. Replaces the old commented-out `actions/cache` block.
- **Cache warming:** the workflow also runs on pushes to `dev`/`main` that touch `frontend/src-tauri/**`, once a week, and on manual dispatch. PRs can only restore caches from their base branch, so without this every new PR would start cold.
- **npm:** `setup-node` caches npm, and installs use `npm ci`.
- **Concurrency:** a new push to a PR cancels that PR's in-progress run.
- **Trigger:** edits to the workflow file now run the build check too.

Normal PRs only restore the cache. A new cache is saved only when `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml` or the toolchain changes, which keeps usage well under the 10 GB repo limit.

### Results

pr_events.title: Add stateful helpers for p5.strands addons
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Resolves #9259

Changes:

Adds `p5.registerStrandsState()` so addons can create independent helpers whose values follow branches and loops. `push()` and `pop()` restore scoped values while global values keep their updates.

The optional `globalInstance` exposes a helper’s methods during a build, then restores the original properties. Nested `modify()` calls are rejected. Errors escaping hook callbacks or `begin()`/`end()` stop code generation, even if the sketch catches them.

Includes addon docs and examples, plus a small WGSL fix needed for matrix state.

+<!-- Guide to translating the p5.js-website content. -->
+
+# Translate the p5.js Website
+
+Translation is a great first contribution if you want to contribute to p5.js. You don't need to understand the whole codebase, instead just the language you are translating into in enough.
+
+This page covers finding a translation task, editing the file, previewing locally, and opening a pull request.
+
+## Table of Contents
+- [Before you begin](#before-you-begin)
+- [Workflow overview](#workflow-overview)
+- [1. Fork and clone](#1-fork-and-clone)
+- [2. Create a branch](#2-create-a-branch)
+- [3. Edit the translation file](#3-edit-the-translation-file)
+- [4. Preview locally](#4-preview-locally)
+- [5. Commit, push, and open a pull request](#5-commit-push-and-open-a-pull-request)
+- [Translation coverage](#translation-coverage)
+
+## Before you begin
+
+1. Read the [Community Statement](https://p5js.org/about/#community-statement).
+2. Create a [GitHub account](https://github.com/signup) if you do not have one.
+3. See the already existing translation issues on [`processing/p5.js-website`](https://github.com/processing/p5.js-website/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22needs+translation%22), and you can pick one to work on.
+4. Comment on the issue with the language you want to work on (for example, Spanish or Hindi). That helps avoid duplicate work.
+
+Issues may mark a translation as **missing** or **outdated**. Follow the file path listed in the issue.
+
+## Workflow overview
+
+```mermaid
+---
+title: Workflow overview of language contribution
+---
+flowchart TD
+    ChooseIssue[Choose a translation issue] --> Comment[Comment with your language]
+    Comment --> ForkClone[Fork and clone p5.js-website]
+    ForkClone --> Edit[Translate the file]
+    Edit --> RemoveFlag[Remove needsTranslation line]
+    RemoveFlag --> Preview[Run npm run dev]
+    Preview --> OpenPR[Open a pull request]
+```
+
+## 1. Fork and clone
+
+1. Open [`processing/p5.js-website`](https://github.com/processing/p5.js-website).
+2. Click **Fork** in the upper-right corner.
+
+The second step to work on the p5.js-website translation code is to fork the p5.js-website repository. Forking has a specific meaning in open source, but for our purpose, it means creating a copy of the repository and storing it in your own GitHub account. To fork a repo, simply click on the "Fork" button near the top of the page, and GitHub will make a copy of the repo in your account.
+
+![Screenshot of the main page of repository. A button, labeled with a fork icon and "Fork 59.3k," is outlined in dark orange.](images/fork.png)
+
+3. Clone your fork 
+
+Once the fork is created, navigate to your fork's page and copy the git URL by clicking the green "Code" button.
+
+![Screenshot of the list of files on the landing page of a repository. The "Code" button is highlighted with a dark orange outline.](images/code-button.png)
+
+Next go to the command line in your local environment and clone this git repository. "Clone" simply means download a copy of the repo to your local machine. Run the following command in a folder where you want to store the p5.js-website source code folder.
+
+```
+git clone [git_url]
+```
+
+Replace `[git_url]` with the URL you just copied above. This can take several minutes, depending on the speed of your internet connection, a good time to make some coffee! Once the process is finished, you can open up the downloaded folder named `p5.js-website` in your preferred text editor and start looking around.
+
+4. Install dependencies:
+
+```bash
+cd p5.js-website
+npm install
+```
+This command helps you move to the right folder, and then install the required dependencies to run the project properly.
+
+## 2. Create a branch
+
+It i

pr_events.title: GUI: Extend --dump-all-dialogs to cover tabs, scroll pages and more dialogs, compatible with web plate
pr_events.body_excerpt:
- gui/dump-all-dialogs.cpp
  - Capture every page of a scroll container, saved as -pageN.
  - Open tabbed dialogs once, because OptionsDialog::open() rebuilds its widgets.
  - Dump every tab of HelpDialog using loopThroughTabs().
  - Dump the remaining dialogs, including DLC, recorder and updates when they are enabled.
  - Keep the original naming and the snapshots/ folder. New dialog names don't have the extra hyphen.
- ScrollContainerWidget: new scroll position accessors, used to page through the contents.
- TabWidget: new getActiveTabWidgets(), used to walk the widgets of the active tab.
- ListWidget: keep at least one entry per page. With a tall font (CJK or Arabic) at a low resolution, such as the shader browser at 320x200 in Japanese, Korean, Chinese or Arabic, the list could be shorter than one line. reflowLayout() then computed zero entries per page and failed its assert. The value is now clamped to one.

pr_events.title: feat(metacall): store self-load into handle, canonicalize paths, and …
pr_events.body_excerpt:
# Description

This pr improves metacall's metacircular self loading by scoping loaded C symbols into a dedicated private handler rather than polluting the global registry. Using the C loader, the API functions are exported to be fetched by other ports.

### Summary of changes:

1. Handle Scoping: allocate and pass `&metacall_self_handle` to `loader_load_from_package()` so that MetaCall's reflected C functions are scoped privately into this handle.

2. Testing Suite: Updated `metacall_c_metacall_test.cpp` with Google Test assertions:
   - `DisabledByDefault`: Asserts `metacall_initialize() == 0`, checks `metacall_handle("c", "metacall") == NULL` and `metacall_handle_self() == NULL`.

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+# Security Handbook
+
+The p5.js project spans three pieces of software: the library, the website, and the editor. In practice, most users and contributors approach these as the same project, although from the perspective of security vulnerabilities they are very different. But because of the perceived interconnection, including a shared responsible disclosure email, policy, and response team/roles, the threat model document is shared.
+
+To report a vulnerability, or to read about our incident response process, see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/processing/p5.js/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
+
+## Inspiration
+
+Inspiration: the [Pillow security handbook](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/latest/handbook/security.html), because it includes:

pr_events.title: IMAGE: INDEO3: Fix garbage on padded frames
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Indeo 3 rounds the coded frame size up to a multiple of 4, so a frame
can be slightly larger than the stream. The scale factor then became
0, which crashed with a division by zero on x86 and drew garbage on
ARM. Crop such frames in the existing upscale path instead.

Seen in whostolehanukkah, where a 169x184 QuickTime video is coded
as 172x184.

pr_events.title: fix(backend): parse space-separated datetimes with microseconds or a tz offset
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Fixes #1597

`extract_datetime` only attempted `datetime.fromisoformat()` when `"T"` was in the date string, then fell back to a strptime format list that had no space-separated microsecond variant (plain or EXIF-style). A capture timestamp using a space separator together with fractional seconds (e.g. `2024-01-15 14:30:45.123456`) or a timezone offset (e.g. `2024-01-15 14:30:45+05:30`) matched nothing and silently returned `None`, losing the photo's capture date.

Attempt `fromisoformat()` unconditionally instead of gating it on `"T"` — it natively handles both separators, fractional seconds and timezone offsets. Kept the one translation this project's Python version still needs (`fromisoformat` doesn't accept a trailing `Z`), and dropped the manual timezone-stripping split on `+`/`-` that used to run first: it discarded any timezone `fromisoformat` could otherwise have kept, and mishandled negative offsets by splitting the date portion's own hyphens.

Also added the space-separated a

pr_events.body_excerpt:
`watcher_util_get_folder_id_if_watched` and `watcher_util_find_closest_parent_folder` compared paths with plain string equality/`startswith`. Windows filesystems are case-insensitive, but `watchfiles` and the stored folder path can report different casing for the same real path (drive letter, path components), so a real file change or folder deletion silently matched no watched folder and never synced.

Fixed by case-folding both sides with `os.path.normcase()` before comparing.

Verified: without the fix, both lookups return `None` for a case-differing but identical real path (e.g. stored `C:\Users\MANAS\Pictures`, reported `c:\users\manas\pictures\...`); with the fix, both correctly resolve to the watched folder.

pr_events.title: db_insert_folders_batch: dedupe folder paths case-insensitively
pr_events.body_excerpt:
`INSERT OR IGNORE` relies on the `folder_path` `UNIQUE` constraint, which is a byte-exact comparison. A subfolder discovered by `os.walk` during a tree add and already registered under different case (a drive letter or path component Windows reports inconsistently) was not recognized as the same row and got inserted again under a fresh `folder_id` — the same real directory ends up registered twice, with duplicate indexing, AI tagging, and face clusters.

Fixed by checking for a case-insensitive match against already-known paths (both previously-committed rows and other paths in the same batch) before inserting, instead of relying solely on the database's byte-exact `UNIQUE` constraint.

Verified against a temp SQLite database: without the fix, registering a folder and then re-registering the same real directory under different case produces 2 rows; with the fix, the duplicate is correctly skipped, for both a cross-batch case-duplicate and a same-batch one (two `os.walk` entries differi

+++ b/backend/app/database/folders.py
@@ -64,9 +64,28 @@ def db_insert_folders_batch(folders_data: List[FolderData]) -> None:

pr_events.title: fix(rb_loader): free return value in rb_loader_port_metacall
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Description
Fixes a memory leak that happens on every MetaCall::metacall call in Ruby port.

The problem was that in

rb_loader_port_metacall (source/loaders/rb_loader/source/rb_loader_port.c)
, the MetaCall value handle returned by metacallv_s was passed to rb_type_serialize (which constructs Ruby objects from it), but was never released with value_type_destroy (result).
As rb_type_serialize constructs native Ruby objects from it, the value was not freed, since it was not known to be owned by Ruby.
## The Fix
value_type_serialize returns Ruby VALUE, which is then stored in rb_result.
After that, value_type_destroy is called to destroy the MetaCall value handle, since it is no longer needed.
The rb_result is then returned.
## Testing
All 13 Ruby CTest targets are passing (100%) ("ctest -VV -R "rb|ruby"").
Valgrind Memcheck on source/ports/rb_port/test/run.rb reports no more definite leaks (7) of value_alloc from rb_loader_port_metacall .

pr_events.title: ACCESS: Fix access.dat generation
pr_events.body_excerpt:
The create_access tool that generates access.dat has multiple issues resulting in about 87% of the current file being junk data, and different compilers producing inconsistent outputs. 

- FONT2_INDEX_SIZE and FONT6x6_INDEX_SIZE both use sizeof() / 2 on 4-byte int arrays, so the tool incorrectly writes 130 entries from 65-entry arrays, and the data itself varies by compiler. This extra data never appears to be read by ScummVM.

- The table end markers of chars and rooms are absolute file offsets, but the table entries are relative to the data segment. Each last char record and last room record is bringing in ~40-50KB of unrelated executable data (also never read).

- Because of this, Martian ends up reading 72 bytes past MM2.EXE EOF. The existing data (0x7459F–0x745E6) shows all 0xCC, indicating an MSVC debug build; these bytes get replaced with 0x00 when running the same code under clang.

pr_events.title: fix(backend): import ClusterId from face_clusters instead of redefining it
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Fixes #1600

`faces.py` defined its own `ClusterId = int`, while `face_clusters.py` defines `ClusterId = str`. Cluster IDs are `uuid4()` strings, the `face_clusters.cluster_id` column is `TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, and every route and schema takes `cluster_id: str` — `faces.py` was the odd one out.

Runtime impact was none (SQLite's INTEGER affinity only converts text that looks numeric, and every id in practice is a uuid4 with hyphens), but it produced a batch of MyPy errors on every call site that passes a real string `cluster_id` into a `faces.py` function typed as `int`.

Import `ClusterId` from `face_clusters.py` instead of redefining it. The two modules don't import each other, so there's no cycle.

Verified: full `test_faces_db.py` suite (42 tests) passes; mypy on `faces.py`/`face_clusters.py` no longer reports any `cluster_id` type mismatches (the pre-existing, unrelated null-union errors in `face_clusters.py` are untouched).

pr_events.title: db_find_parent_folder_id: match the parent folder case-insensitively

The lookup compared paths with a byte-exact SQL `=`, so a subfolder whose path differs from its already-registered parent only by case (a drive letter or path component the OS/file picker reported with different casing on Windows, which is case-insensitive) found no parent and got linked as a top-level folder instead of nested under its real parent.

Verified against the real function with a temp SQLite database: without the fix, looking up the parent of `c:\users\manas\pictures\Vacation2024` against a stored parent path of `C:\Users\MANAS\Pictures` returns `None`; with the fix, it correctly resolves to the parent's `folder_id`.

pr_events.title: db_folder_exists: match the stored folder path case-insensitively
pr_events.body_excerpt:
A byte-exact SQL `=` missed an already-registered folder whose stored path differs only by case — a drive letter or path component the OS/file picker reported differently on Windows, which is case-insensitive. The add-folder 409 check that calls this never fired, and the same real directory could be inserted a second time since the table's `UNIQUE` constraint is binary too.

Fixed by comparing with `os.path.normcase()` instead of relying on the database's byte-exact match.

Verified against the real function with a temp SQLite database: without the fix, checking whether `c:\users\manas\pictures` exists against a stored row of `C:\Users\MANAS\Pictures` returns `False`; with the fix, it correctly returns `True`.

pr_events.body_excerpt:
Box2D has a global object `b2_defaultFilter` which, having virtual methods, cannot easily be made `constexpr`. Thus it causes global ctor/dtor warnings.

The global object is replaced with an instance-local member. The increase in memory and runtime cost is marginal.
As the object in question has no data members or state (besides the vftable) there is no relevant global state which would have been shared across the program.

The new function `SetDefaultContactFilter()` is unused right now, but present to indicate the express possibility of this operation - previously this could have been done by `SetContactFilter(&b2_defaultFilter)`.

Using `Common::Singleton` in this foreign code looks like the wrong approach here.

pr_events.title: sync logger_writer: split multi-line write() calls into separate log records
pr_events.body_excerpt:
`LoggerWriter.write()` only split on a trailing newline, so a single `write()` call carrying several lines (`print()` of an already multi-line string, a library writing a multi-line block to stdout/stderr in one call) was logged as one record with embedded newlines instead of one record per line.

Fixed by splitting the buffer on every newline, not just a trailing one, so each complete line becomes its own log record while any trailing partial line stays buffered for the next write — matching the intent the existing code already documented ("Buffer the message until we get a complete line" / "Log the complete line").

Verified: without the fix, `write('line one\nline two\nline three\n')` produces one log record containing literal embedded newlines; with the fix, it produces three separate records. A write split across two calls (`write('foo')` then `write('bar\n')`) still correctly logs one record (`'foobar'`).

pr_events.title: IOS7: Fix resize of game screen on virtual keyboard hide/show
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Users reported a problem changing orientation of their devices, from landscape to portrait, that the game screen gets the wrong constraints. The problem became worse the more they changed the orientation of the device.

The resizeParentFrame:keyboardDidShow: function based the game screen size on the reported size of the keyboard frame in the notification. The game screen height was subtracted with the height of the keyboard screen when the keyboard became visible. The height was stored and was added to the game screen height when the keyboard became hidden.

The notifications could be sent one or several times, reporting different frame sizes. The accessory window added some extra complexity.

Since the implementation was based on relative arimethic it was quite fragile. If the reported heights were inconsistent the screen eventually became incorrect.

Make sure to restore the game screen to the full container size when the keyboard is hidden. Also simplify the logic to calculate how

pr_events.title: fix: createRadio().disable(false) does not re-enable radio inputs
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Summary
- Fixes `createRadio().disable(false)` not re-enabling radio inputs
- Root cause: `setAttribute('disabled', false)` sets the attribute to the string "false", which HTML still treats as "present" so the input stays disabled
- Fix: use the DOM property (`radioInput.disabled = shouldDisable`) instead of `setAttribute`, which correctly toggles enable/disable

## Test plan
- Added a unit test that disables then re-enables radio inputs and verifies they are enabled
- Existing disable test still passes

Closes #9316

pr_events.title: fix: refresh outdated Nearby places by removing old cache entries
pr_events.body_excerpt:
**Description (required)**

Fixes #7172  

What changes did you make and why?

Nearby saves the details of each place in the local database. In `loadCachedPlaces()`, a place found in this cache was never fetched again from Wikidata, only places missing from the cache were fetched. So, when an item changes on Wikidata after it was cached, the app keeps showing the old details which make it show shows a normal red pin instead of a red X. This is what happens with Q48765723 in the issue: "dissolved, abolished or demolished date: unknown value" was added on 29 August, so a phone that had cached it before still shows a normal red pin instead of a red X.
The app query already handles "unknown value" correctly: `query_for_item.rq` returns a value for `?destroyed` for both items in the issue, so `Place.from()` sets `exists = false`.
With this change, cached places are still shown right away from the cache, but every place is also fetched again. When the fresh details arrive, the existing code

## Overview

1. This PR fixes #27814.
2. This PR does the following: Removes the duplicate `const blogUrl = testConstants.URLs.Blog;` declaration from `core/tests/playwright-acceptance-tests/utilities/user/logged-out-user.ts` on `develop`. This is a one-line deletion; nothing else is changed.
3. (For bug-fixing PRs only) The original bug occurred because: #27597 (view-the-blog, line 28) and #27505 (interested-donor, line 216) each added the same `blogUrl` constant to `logged-out-user.ts`. Each PR was fine on its own, but after both merged, `develop` declares `blogUrl` twice, so the file fails to load:

   ```text
   SyntaxError: Identifier 'blogUrl' has already been declared
   ```

   Every Playwright spec imports `LoggedOutUser` (through `user-factory.ts`), so on any PR that merges the latest `develop`, all Playwright acceptance suites start and then run 0 tests (`0 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`) and fail. Some examples from other PRs:

pr_events.title: test: keep the debouncer startup test out of the real thumbnails directory (#1607)
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Closes #1607

## Root cause

`test_startup_creates_and_shutdown_closes_the_debouncer` in `backend/tests/test_metadata_export_pipeline.py` is the only test that imports `main`. `main.py` runs `os.makedirs(THUMBNAIL_IMAGES_PATH, exist_ok=True)` at module level (line 75), and `settings.py` builds that path from `user_data_dir("PictoPy")` unconditionally. The `GITHUB_ACTIONS` guard in `conftest.py` redirects the database only, so every local run creates `thumbnails/` in the real PictoPy user data directory.

## Fix

The test now points `THUMBNAIL_IMAGES_PATH` at a `tmp_path` directory before `import main`. It uses `monkeypatch.setattr`, as the other tests that patch this path already do (10 sites across `test_images_delete.py`, `test_images_rescan.py` and `test_videos.py`). Those tests patch the module that uses the name. Here the patch has to land on `app.config.settings`, because `main` copies the name from there while it is being imported.

One test changes. No app code changes.

## Evi

## Description
Resolves memory leak issues in the Python loader detected by Valgrind.

Under standard runtime execution, CPython's default allocator (`obmalloc`) can obscure individual allocations and report false positives. When profiled with deterministic allocation (`PYTHONMALLOC=malloc` / debug symbols), this patch ensures zero memory leaks within MetaCall's loader execution path.

## Valgrind Comparison

| State | Contexts / Leak Summary |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Before** | 250 contexts (allocator noise / unsuppressed caches) |
| **After** | ~50 contexts (clean deterministic profile, leaks resolved) |

*(Attach your "Before" and "After" screenshot images here)*

- [x] Test suite passes cleanly (`metacall-python-testd`)
- [x] Valgrind memcheck verified

pr_events.title: Fix paletteLerp() returning undefined outside p5.strands
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Resolves #9328

Changes:
- `paletteLerp()` returned `undefined` outside p5.strands because the strands override returned early without calling the original CPU implementation. The override now saves the original `paletteLerp` and delegates to it when no strands context is active, the same pattern `lerpColor` uses.
- Adds a regression test that calls `paletteLerp()` outside strands and checks the interpolated color. It fails without the fix (`undefined`) and passes with it.
- Strands behavior and the `argTypes` metadata are unchanged, and the existing `paletteLerp` and `argTypes` tests still pass.

This regression came from #8817. Targeting the 2.4 milestone.

pr_events.title: SCI: GK1: Add option for high-resolution text
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Fixes [#17355](https://bugs.scummvm.org/ticket/17355) "SCI: GK1: High resolution graphics mode scales text and low-res graphics unevenly (200→480 vertical stretch)"

Normally, when "Enable high resolution graphics" is enabled, GK1 stretches low-resolution text by 12/5 vertically, so source rows alternate between 2 and 3 pixels tall (in a 3, 2, 3, 2, 2 pattern), an ugly upscaling.

When the new "Enable high resolution text" is enabled, text is rendered at its native 2x size, without ugly upscaling.

pr_events.title: fix(color): stop re-wrapping p5.Color for every sketch
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Resolves #9299

Changes:

Every new sketch wrapped the `p5.Color` methods again. Removed sketches stayed in memory, and `red()`, `green()`, `blue()` and `alpha()` could use the ranges of the wrong sketch.

- `red()`, `green()`, `blue()` and `alpha()` now pass their ranges, like #8062 did for `hue()`.
- The setters use `registerDecorator` once. Each color keeps a link to its sketch. A `remove` hook clears that link.
- `setAlpha()` now uses the alpha range of the color's mode. This fixes the HSB case from the issue.

Added `test/unit/color/instances.js`.

pr_events.body_excerpt:
# Description

fixes the pre-push hook on clones that don't have tags (like forks). `git rev-list --tags` comes back empty, `git describe` fails, and the hook ended up writing an empty VERSION, committing it and creating a `v` tag. now it exits early when there's no tag to compare against.

Fixes #939

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

# Checklist:

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [x] tested the hook by hand in throwaway clones:
  - no tags: exits 0, VERSION untouched (before the fix: VERSION emptied, junk commit and a `v` tag)
  - tags matching VERSION: exits 0
  - tag newer than VERSION: still updates VERSION and rejects the push like before
- [ ] ctest / docker / sanitizers: not run, only a shell hook changed
- [ ] `make clang-format`: not needed, no C/C++ changes
- [x] linked issue: #939

+# Pull request scope check
+
+The `Check Pull Request Scope` workflow uses a configurable OpenAI-compatible
+provider and a deterministic fallback.
+
+## Configure the AI provider
+
+Set the repository **Actions secret**:
+
+- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
+
+The workflow uses OpenRouter with the model
+`nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free`. Provider rate limits and free-tier
+availability can change.
+
+For pull requests from forks, GitHub does not provide repository secrets to
+the workflow. When no API key is available or the provider is unavailable,
+the rule-based fallback runs. It only logs a notice about a missing title,
+missing description, or unchecked checklist item. It cannot judge whether
+changes are related, always returns `no`, and never posts a comment. Do not
+change this workflow to `pull_request_target` or run pull request code with
+secrets.
+
+## Fallback and disabling AI
+
+Set the repository Actions variable `AI_PROVIDER=none` to disable API calls
+and run only the rule-based fallback. The fallback logs notices for a missing
+title, missing description, or unchecked Markdown task-list item. It cannot
+determine whether code changes are genuinely related to the PR, always
+returns `no`, and never posts a comment.
+
+To disable the entire workflow, disable **Check Pull Request Scope** from the
+repository's Actions settings or remove its `pull_request` trigger.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+provider="${1:?provider is required}"
+base_url="${2:-}"
+model="${3:-}"
+prompt="${4:-}"
+api_key="${AI_API_KEY:-}"
+title="${PR_TITLE:-}"
+body="${PR_BODY:-}"
+
+write_output() {
+  local name="$1"
+  local value="$2"
+  if [[ -n "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}" ]]; then
+    printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$value" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+  fi
+}
+
+run_rules() {
+  local reason=""
+  if [[ -z "${title//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
+    reason="missing-title"
+  elif [[ -z "${body//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
+    reason="missing-description"
+  elif printf '%s\n' "$body" | grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*[-*+][[:space:]]+\[[[:space:]]\]'; then
+    reason="unchecked-checklist"
+  fi
+
+  # The rule-based fallback cannot judge whether changes are related, so it
+  # never answers "yes" (which would post an "unrelated changes" comment).
+  local response="no"
+  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
+    echo "::notice::Rule-based fallback noticed '${reason}' but cannot judge relevance; no comment will be posted."
+  fi
+  write_output response "$response"
+  write_output mode rules
+  write_output reason "$reason"
+  printf '%s\n' "$response"
+}
+
+case "$provider" in
+  none)
+    echo "::notice::AI scope check disabled by AI_PROVIDER=none; using the rule-based fallback."
+    run_rules
+    exit 0
+    ;;
+  openrouter)
+    ;;
+  *)
+    echo "::error::Unsupported AI_PROVIDER: $provider"
+    exit 1
+    ;;
+esac
+
+if [[ -z "$api_key" ]]; then
+  echo "::notice::AI scope check skipped: no API key available"
+  run_rules
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+if [[ -z "$model" ]]; then
+  echo "::error::AI scope check requires an OpenRouter model."
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+base_url="${base_url%/}"
+case "$provider:$base_url" in
+  openrouter:https://openrouter.ai/api/v1)
+    if [[ "$model" != *:free ]]; then
+      echo "::error::OpenRouter model ID must end in :free."
+      exit 1
+    fi
+    ;;
+  *)
+    echo "::error::Unsupported base URL for provider $provider."
+    exit 1
+    ;;
+esac
+
+request_file="$(mktemp)"
+response_file="$(mktemp)"
+trap 'rm -f "$request_file" "$response_file"' EXIT
+

pr_events.title: SHERLOCK: Reduce resource library memory usage
pr_events.body_excerpt:
The Sherlock engine keeps complete library files in memory instead of reading only the required resources from storage when needed. This is especially a problem on systems with limited memory, for example the Wii.

My change reads only the indexes with the position and size of the contained resources from uncompressed library files and keeps this information in memory. When a resource is requested, only this resource is read from storage. Compressed library files are still kept in memory.

With this change, Holmes 2 can be played on the Wii.

I tested the following games on both PC and Wii:

Holmes 1 - PC - English
Holmes 1 - PC - English with German patch
Holmes 1 - 3DO - English
Holmes 2 - PC - German

Smooth turning starts once the original would have made a walker for the actor, the first time it walks, turns, or follows boxes. Before that, SetActorRot sets the rotation at once.

## What this does
Fixes #1668.

The two toggles in the **System** settings card ("Launch at startup" and "Close to tray") were hand-built with `<button role="switch">` and custom Tailwind classes, instead of the shared `Switch` component (`components/ui/switch`) that every other toggle in the app uses. This swaps them to the shared `<Switch>` so all toggles are consistent.

- `SystemSettingsCard.tsx`: replaced the two custom `<button role="switch">` toggles with the shared `<Switch>` component.

pr_events.title: [ai] mattermost: Improve conversion of threaded discussions during import
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Problem

The Mattermost importer previously dumped all thread replies flat in the main channel topic (`imported from mattermost`), losing thread context entirely. Users importing from Mattermost couldn't distinguish thread replies from regular messages, and thread structure was completely lost.

## Solution

Implemented a two-pass processing pipeline matching the Slack importer pattern:

1. **Pass 1**: Pre-scan messages to count replies and build thread metadata map
2. **Pass 2**: Route messages based on thread structure:
   - Thread parent messages stay in the main import topic with a cross-linking notice: `*N replies in #**stream>thread_topic***`
   - Thread replies go to dedicated thread topics named `YYYY-MM-DD <snippet> (N)`

## Changes

- `zerver/data_import/mattermost.py`: Added thread helper functions (`is_mattermost_thread_parent`, `get_mattermost_thread_key`, `count_mattermost_thread_replies`), two-pass processing in `process_posts()`, and thread-aware routing in `process_

+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        user_id: str,
+        intent: str,
+        role: Optional[str] = None,
+        username: Optional[str] = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Initializes an audit payload without storage metadata.
+
+        Args:
+            user_id: str. The acting or affected user ID supplied by the caller.
+            intent: str. The role action being recorded.
+            role: str|None. The exact role value supplied by the caller.
+            username: str|None. The exact username value or query.
+        """
+        self.user_id = user_id
+        self.intent = intent
+        self.role = role
+        self.username = username
+
+    def validate(self) -> None:
+        """Validates the payload format without looking up current users.
+
+        Raises:
+            ValidationError. A property has an invalid type or value.
+        """
+        if not isinstance(self.user_id, str):
+            raise utils.ValidationError(
+                'user_id must be a string, but got %r' % self.user_id
+            )
+        # The shared helper matches a prefix; the length check excludes suffixes.
+        if len(self.user_id) != feconf.USER_ID_LENGTH or not (
+            utils.is_user_id_valid(self.user_id)
+        ):
+            raise utils.ValidationError(
+                'user_id=%r has the wrong format' % self.user_id
+            )
+        if not isinstance(self.intent, str):
+            raise utils.ValidationError(
+                'intent must be a string, but got %r' % self.intent
+            )
+        if self.intent not in (
+            feconf.ROLE_ACTION_ADD,
+            feconf.ROLE_ACTION_REMOVE,
+            feconf.ROLE_ACTION_VIEW_BY_ROLE,
+            feconf.ROLE_ACTION_VIEW_BY_USERNAME,
+        ):
+            raise utils.ValidationError(
+                'Invalid role-query intent: %s' % self.intent
+            )
+        if self.role is not None and not isinstance(self.role, str):
+            raise utils.ValidationError(
+                'role must be a string or None, but got %r' % self.role
+            )
+        if self.username is not None and not isinstance(self.username, str):
+            raise utils.ValidationError(
+                'username must be a string or None, but got %r' % self.username
+            )

Custom profile field operations should be recorded in the realm audit log so that administrators' changes can be tracked.

pr_events.title: Fix SVG currentColor inheritance from active p5 styles (#9246)
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Resolves #9246

Changes:

### Context & Problem
During SVG import (`loadSVG()` or `createSVG()`), elements using `fill="currentColor"` or `stroke="currentColor"` defaulted to solid black (`rgb(0, 0, 0)`). This happened because `RenderContext.color` was initialized to black, so `makeColor()` resolved `currentColor` to black immediately during import.

When the imported shape was played back using `shape()`, the importer's hardcoded fill and stroke calls overrode the canvas drawing state, preventing users from styling icon SVGs with active `fill()` and `stroke()` calls.

### Solution
1. **Differentiate missing color from explicit black (`src/shape/svg/svg_import.js`)**:
   - Initialized `RenderContext.color = null;` instead of `"rgb(0, 0, 0)"`.
   - In `ShapeBuilder.prototype.makeColor()`, if `currentColor` is used:
     - If an ancestor or element `color` exists, it resolves to that color.
     - If no `color` is defined in the SVG, it stores the `"currentColor"` marker string on the sh

pr_events.title: fix(strands): preserve loop state updated before break
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Resolves #9327

Loop state was only written back at the end of the loop body, so a `break` could exit with the value from the start of that iteration.

This updates the Strands loop handling so the current carried values are committed before `break`.

Changes:
- Pass the loop's carried values to `break` before control-flow renaming, so they resolve to the live value at the break site.
- Commit those values to the innermost `StrandsFor` before emitting the break.
- Add WebGL and WebGPU regression tests covering updates before break, assignments in the breaking branch, and nested loops.

Tested on both WebGL and WebGPU.

pr_events.title: Fix storage element type check and FES parameter data for createStorage/buildComputeShader
pr_events.body_excerpt:
This is a follow up to #9083, I found this while testing **v2.4.0-rc.2**

The mismatch warning from #9083 never actually fired. #9086 widened the storage regex for StorageList, so it now grabs the whole type like `array<atomic<u32>>` instead of just `atomic<u32>`, and the type lookup returned nothing. My old tests mocked the parsed object so they missed it.

Fixed it by unwrapping `array<T>` / `array<T, N>` to get the element type. once that worked, StorageLists in render shaders started hitting the check and crashed since they don't have `_arrayType`, which broke `instances(storageList)`. Lists only hold floats or structs so the check just skips them now.

Also `parameterData.json` was never regenerated after #9083, so `createStorage(new Uint32Array(...))` gave a false FES warning. And `buildComputeShader()` only listed a function param, so the hooks object form from the reference logged a raw zod error. I added the missing overloads and updated just those 3 entries

pr_events.title: [ai] provision: Fix PGroonga failing to load on Debian 13.
pr_events.body_excerpt:
On Debian 13, we build PGroonga from source against libgroonga-dev from packages.groonga.org. Its libgroonga0 16.1.5-1 depends on libarrow2600, which links against the OpenTelemetry C++ libraries without declaring a dependency on them. So provisioning fails in postgresql-init-dev-db, because PostgreSQL cannot load pgroonga.so without libopentelemetry_exporter_otlp_http_log.so.

Fix this by installing opentelemetry-cpp from Debian's main archive. Ubuntu 26.04 also builds PGroonga from source, but against Ubuntu's own libgroonga-dev, so it is not affected.

- https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/55112
- Bug report on CZO: https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/31-production-help/topic/.5BZulip.2012.2E3.5D.20django.20crashing.20after.20libgroonga0.20update/with/2545976

pr_events.title: [ai] message_store: Prep for anchoring topic links on their permalink's message.
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Prep work split out of #40503 (anchoring topic links on their permalink's message), so that PR can be reviewed as the four commits that change behavior. None of these depend on each other or on that PR.

- `hash_util: Reject non-numeric message ids in channel/topic links.` A standalone fix: `decode_stream_topic_from_url` accepted any operand after `near`, and `save_topic_links` parsed it with `Number.parseInt`, so a malformed link such as `/near/abc` was tracked under message id `NaN`.
- `message_store: Use util.StreamTopic for narrow parameters.` Type-only.
- `message_store: Rename refile helpers to say they act on pending links.` `refile_links_to_message` and `refile_link_from_message` only handle links whose target wasn't in the store yet, which the names didn't say.
- `message_store tests: Build expected topic links with helpers.` A pure refactor of the test expectations onto `message_link`/`topic_link` helpers, which #40503 then extends with a field.

pr_events.title: desktop_notifications: Drop unneeded close() in the startup check.
pr_events.body_excerpt:
A notification constructed without permission is never shown, so the startup check has no need to close it.

This also helps non-standard clients whose Notification objects lack close() (we noticed a few such clients in sentry). There, the call threw and the web app failed to load.

Such clients don't follow the spec, so we don't promise that notifications work there. But the web app now loads.

pr_events.title: stream_settings: Optimize DOM queries in redraw_left_panel.
pr_events.body_excerpt:
### Summary of changes
This PR optimizes DOM queries in `redraw_left_panel` within `web/src/stream_settings_ui.ts`.

In organizations with hundreds of channels, opening the channel management overlay or switching tabs suffered from redundant DOM lookups:
- `$("#channels_overlay_container .stream-row")` was queried twice from the DOM.
- Inside the loop appending stream rows, `scroll_util.get_content_element($("#channels_overlay_container .streams-list"))` was repeatedly re-evaluated on every iteration (300+ times).

We now cache `$rows` and `$streams_list_content` outside the loops, eliminating hundreds of redundant DOM selector queries during redraws.

Contributes towards #39755.

### Testing done
- Ran `./tools/test-js-with-node web/tests/stream_settings_ui.test.cjs` (passed).
- Ran full node test suite `./tools/test-js-with-node` (all 188 modules passed).
- Ran `./tools/lint web/src/stream_settings_ui.ts` (0 errors, 0 warnings).

pr_events.body_excerpt:
**Description**
This PR resolves a nil-pointer dereference runtime panic in `CloneMesheryPatternHandler` and `CloneMesheryFilterHandler` when requests have an empty resource ID (`patternID == ""` or `filterID == ""`) alongside a valid JSON payload.

Per maintainer direction:
1. Validates `patternID` and `filterID` upfront before decoding `r.Body`, returning HTTP 400 Bad Request immediately if missing.
2. Decouples request body decoding into a separate step.
3. Defensively guards `ErrRequestBody` against `nil` error values to prevent calling `.Error()` on `nil`.
4. Adds regression tests to `server/handlers/meshery_pattern_handler_test.go` asserting HTTP 400 on empty resource ID without panics.

pr_events.title: Fix initialization of documented_commands dictionary
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Pull request that solves issue #40544 
In `manage.py`, line 31 initialises `documented_commands` using `dict()` rather than the dictionary literal `{}`.

Why change it?

1. Ruff compliance: Zulip’s `pyproject.toml` enables Ruff rule `C408`, which flags the unnecessary `dict()` call.
2. Style consistency: The surrounding code uses literals for empty collections, such as `{ }` for `documented_command_subsets` and `[ ]` for lists.
3. Efficiency: i have tested in local across 10 million iterations in standard CPython.  { } took 0.285 seconds versus 0.428 seconds for dict( ) which is about 33.4% less CPU time. That’s roughly 14.3 ns saved per call.

Proposed change:  Replace `documented_commands = dict( )` with `documented_commands = { }`.

I have tested this change locally.

pr_events.title: [Docker Extension] Fix nil-pointer panic in proxy ServeHTTP
pr_events.body_excerpt:
**Notes for Reviewers**

This PR fixes #22664.

`install/docker-extension/vm/proxy/proxy.go` dereferenced a nil value on two error paths in `ServeHTTP`:

- When `client.Do(req)` returned an error, the handler wrote a 500 but did **not** `return`, so `defer resp.Body.Close()` (and `resp.Status` / `resp.Header` / `resp.StatusCode`) ran on a nil `resp` → panic whenever the Meshery server was unreachable.
- On the `/ws` path, `ws.SetCloseHandler(...)` and `go handleWsMessage(ws)` ran **before** the `upgrader.Upgrade(...)` error was checked, so a failed upgrade used a nil `ws` → panic.

`go vet` and `staticcheck` do not catch either one.

**Changes**
- Return immediately after writing the 500 when `client.Do` fails, so the nil response is never dereferenced.
- Check the `upgrader.Upgrade` error right away and return before using `ws`.
- Added regression tests (`install/docker-extension/vm/proxy/proxy_test.go`) covering both paths.

pr_events.body_excerpt:
**Notes for Reviewers**

This PR fixes #22684.

`.github/workflows/auto-merge-meeting-minutes.yml` auto-approves and auto-merges a PR to `master` (using a token that bypasses branch protection) when every changed file is under `docs/meetings/`. The check called `pulls.listFiles({ per_page: 100 })` and iterated a **single page**, so a PR with more than 100 changed files was only validated on its first 100 — files beyond position 100 were never checked and could fall outside `docs/meetings/` yet still be auto-merged.

- Enumerate **all** changed files with `github.paginate(github.rest.pulls.listFiles, …)`.

- **Fail closed** if a PR reaches the `listFiles` enumeration ceiling (3000 files), since it can't be fully inspected.

pr_events.title: Make media elements and createCapture() work in WebGPU
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Resolves https://github.com/processing/p5.js/issues/9357

Changes:
- Handles some `readyState` values of media elements that WebGL natively seems to just handle but that we need to explicitly handle in WebGPU. Basically just waiting to actually draw stuff until it's ready
- Handles what seems to be a current Firefox limitation where WebGPU doesn't support video elements as textures yet. Presumably this will work in the future. But in the mean time if we see this fail, we catch the error and fall back to drawing the video through a canvas first. So this should just start doing the more efficient thing in Firefox when that works.
- Handles element source size changing dynamically. When it first goes through it has size 0 because the stream isn't available yet, but then this size gets cached and never changes. So now WebGPU looks for this and makes a new texture when it happens.

pr_events.title: [ai] requirements: Upgrade brotli and brotlicffi for security fix.
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Upgrades `brotli` to 1.2.1 and `brotlicffi` to 1.2.1.0, which fix an out-of-bounds write in the decoder ([GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35)).

Fixes: Security advisory above; no issue filed.

In our lockfile, both packages are only pulled in by `scrapy` (`brotli` on CPython, `brotlicffi` on PyPy). That makes them development-only dependencies, used by the documentation link crawler, rather than part of the production server, so the practical exposure is low.

The lock was regenerated with `uv lock --upgrade-package brotli --upgrade-package brotlicffi`. Newer `uv` also reorders the resolution markers, which is a no-op, so the commit keeps the original order to keep the diff to the two packages.

An encrypted message can quote itself or form a cycle through other messages. Recursive decryption did not reduce the quote depth, so these chains could request the same messages repeatedly.

+# E2EE search backend contract
+
+The optional `e2eeSearch` bridge provides a local index. An absent bridge does not authorize a browser fallback inside a desktop app.
+
+## Compatibility
+
+Existing backends keep `search(query): Promise<E2EESearchHit[]>`. Its default behavior does not change.
+
+Recent pagination requires `searchRecentPage`, `onIndexEvent`, and `close`. The open result must announce all three version-1 capabilities. A consumer must check both the capabilities and the methods before it uses this path.
+
+A partial or absent capability report does not provide the new contract. Existing desktop versions must keep their current search behavior.
+
+## Recent pagination
+
+`searchRecentPage` orders matching hits by descending `ts`, then descending binary `id`. SQLite backends use binary text collation. Other backends must use the same UTF-8 byte order, not locale-dependent sorting.
+
+A cursor has both the timestamp and ID of the last returned hit. The next page selects older timestamps, or smaller IDs at the same timestamp.
+
+The backend applies every original filter to every page. A changed filter starts a new query without a cursor. The backend returns `nextCursor` only when another matching hit exists.
+
+The cursor does not provide snapshot isolation during index changes. A consumer restarts its query after a `changed` event. Relevance pagination is outside this method.
+
+## Shared limits
+
+`E2EE_SEARCH_LIMITS` defines backend result, query-token, document, and batch limits. Both client batching and backend input checks must use these limits.
+
+Document and batch body limits count UTF-16 code units. They do not count encoded bytes. The client can have a separate total-result limit across several backend pages.
+
+## Open sessions and events
+
+An open result with `locked: true` creates no index and writes nothing. Search and mutation methods reject while locked.
+
+A `lost` event invalidates crawler checkpoints for the affected open index. A `changed` event invalidates displayed search results.
+
+Each listener belongs to the open session that registered it. A consumer unsubscribes before closing or replacing that session. It ignores callbacks from an old session.
+
+`close` ends active access and releases resources. It does not imply deletion or a retention policy. Explicit clear uses `wipe`.
+
+## Conformance
+
+`tests/recentPages.contract.ts` provides a backend test for 205 matching timestamp ties. Run it against each backend implementation. A test of the shared types alone does not prove backend behavior.
+
+Backend checks must also cover invalid cursors, limits, locked storage, index loss, listener cleanup, and legacy capability handling.

## Summary

Browsers need a local backend to search decrypted messages without sending the index or queries to the server. This adds a SQLite/WASM worker, encrypted snapshots, and tab coordination behind the shared search contract. It does not activate search or add the client UI.

- **Durability and capacity:** Mutations await snapshot persistence rather than acknowledge a delayed save. This adds save latency per accepted mutation or batch. Representative capacity remains unmeasured.
- **Product:** Memory-only operation remains available when persistent storage is unavailab

pr_events.title: fix: handle rejected scheduled cache synchronization
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Summary

A scheduled cache synchronization can reject during logout or key reset. The timer awaited synchronization and save operations without a failure handler, so either rejection could escape the background task.

## What changed

- **The scheduled task handles sync and save failures.** `CachedStore.trySync` logs the error at the timer owner. Shared `sync` behavior and reset endpoint error handling stay unchanged.
- **Existing retry triggers remain unchanged.** A false sync result schedules another attempt. Token rotation does not cancel the pending synchronization, because it need not produce another login event.

pr_events.title: feat: search encrypted room messages in the local client index
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Summary

Users need to search messages that only an unlocked E2EE client can decrypt. This connects the local index to message decryption, synchronization, account controls, and room search without sending search terms or the index to the server.

The client still requests encrypted history and deletion records from the server. This PR depends on the separate server, model, bridge, browser, and correctness prerequisites. It does not replace their existing PRs.

## Decisions to validate

- **Security:** Proposed KW1 derivation uses HKDF-SHA-256 with the private key's JWK exponent, a fixed label, and user ID. Derivation review remains open. Storage tests are not security approval.
- **Product:** Proposed admin permission and device consent both default to off. Consent belongs to the canonical workspace URL and user. Logout retains consent and sealed data, while consent withdrawal deletes the scoped index.
- **Synchronization:** Proposed indexing catches up changes before older history

pr_events.title: [ai] queue: Fix duplicate sends when workers are stopped mid-batch.
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Fixes: Users receiving duplicate email notifications after the server's queue workers are restarted.

When supervisor stops or restarts a queue worker (deploys, upgrades,
`supervisorctl restart`), the worker exited immediately, even partway
through a batch. RabbitMQ then redelivered the entire batch after the
restart, including events that had already been processed. For the
`email_senders` queue, which processes up to 100 emails per batch, users
received those emails twice.

**Single-process workers** (first commit): the SIGTERM handler called
`sys.exit` in the middle of the batch callback, so the batch was nacked
and requeued. SIGTERM and SIGINT now just set a flag, which the consume
loop checks after the current batch has been acknowledged. The loop also
wakes at least once a second when idle, so it notices the flag.

**Threaded workers** (second commit; the default on servers with less
than ~3.8GB of RAM): `--multi_threaded` ran under Django's autoreload,
apparently copied from the

## Proposed changes (including videos or screenshots)

Converts eight leaf workspace packages from CommonJS to pure ESM: `@rocket.chat/random`, `base64`, `sha256`, `emitter`, `favicon`, `memo`, `poplib` and `password-policies`. Nothing else in the monorepo has to change for them.

Each commit can be reviewed on its own:

1. **Drop stale Storybook ranges from `yarn.lock`.** Running `yarn` on `develop` removes two ranges nothing requires anymore (`@storybook/react@^9.1.21` and `storybook@^9.1.21`). It's unrelated to the rest and can be dropped or merged separately.
2. **Map relative `.js` imports to sources in the Jest presets.** ESM sources import relative files with explicit `.js` extensions, and jest-resolve doesn't map them back to `.ts` the way TypeScript does. Both the server and client presets now do.
3. **One `refactor: convert … to pure ESM` commit per package.** Each package:
   - gets `"type": "module"` and an `exports` map with `types` and `default` conditions. `random` also

## Proposed changes (including videos or screenshots)

`docs/change-organization.md` was being read, by agents above all, as "every fix and refactor is its own pull request, right now". The result was stacks of tiny pull requests chained on each other's branches (a `+8/-1` type overload opened as its own pull request, a dozen pull requests opened within half an hour), each needing its own review, rebase and green CI. `docs/database-access.md` made it worse by turning every nearby inline query into a mandatory refactor pull request.

The goal stays the same: a feature that takes long to validate must not hold fixes and refactors hostage, nor stall behind one huge review. The way there changes:

- **Start from a clear definition.** The draft body says what is wanted, why, what is out of scope and how to tell it works. No formal spec. It keeps a list of the decisions a person made and the open gaps. A choice an agent made on its own stays under gaps until a person confirms it. Feature not

pr_events.title: docs: propose replacing typia with Zod for runtime schemas
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Proposed changes

Adds [`docs/proposals/typia-to-zod.md`](https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/blob/docs/typia-to-zod-proposal/docs/proposals/typia-to-zod.md), a proposal to replace typia with Zod for runtime schemas, and lists it in the `CLAUDE.md` docs index. No code changes.

Opened as a draft so people can read it and comment before any implementation starts.

**Summary**
- typia lives in two packages. `core-typings` generates 222 JSON Schema components (37 entity types) used by 124 REST response `$ref`s. `ui-kit` has 20 `createIs` guards that nothing calls.
- typia keeps both packages on `ttsc` + TypeScript 5.9 (a TS7 blocker), needs a yarn patch, and needs `normalizeForAjv2020` to fix its output for Ajv 2020.
- `z.toJSONSchema` emits the Ajv 2020 dialect directly, and `core-typings` already has Zod-first types.
- Trap: `z.custom` (e.g. `IBanner.view`) can't be represented and silently weakens validation. A type moves only when everything it reaches has a real Zod schema,

 - [docs/proposals/](docs/proposals/) — design proposals, not yet implemented
   - [serve-client-without-meteor-webapp.md](docs/proposals/serve-client-without-meteor-webapp.md) — serving the client without Meteor's `web.browser` program
   - [finish-moving-http-and-ddp-off-meteor.md](docs/proposals/finish-moving-http-and-ddp-off-meteor.md) — what still reaches Meteor's HTTP and DDP servers, and the order to move it
+  - [typia-to-zod.md](docs/proposals/typia-to-zod.md) — replacing typia with Zod for the REST component schemas and the UiKit guards, one type at a time
diff --git a/docs/proposals/typia-to-zod.md b/docs/proposals/typia-to-zod.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000..d6c7dd1fd8005
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/proposals/typia-to-zod.md
@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+# Proposal: replace typia with Zod for runtime schemas
+
+Status: proposed, not implemented. Open for comments.
+
+## Context
+
+typia is a compile-time transform: it reads TypeScript types and emits validators or JSON Schema. Two packages use it.
+
+- **`@rocket.chat/core-typings`**: `src/Ajv.ts` calls `typia.json.schemas<[…]>('3.1')` over 37 entity types
+  (`IMessage`, `IUser`, `IRoom`, `ISubscription`, …). The result is 222 components, about 166 KB of JSON. The REST
+  layer registers them in Ajv (`apps/meteor/server/api/validation/ajv.ts`) and in the OpenAPI document
+  (`apps/meteor/server/api/default/openApi.ts`). Response schemas point at them through 124 `$ref`s;
+  `IMessage` alone has 30.
+- **`@rocket.chat/ui-kit`**: 20 `typia.createIs<…>()` guards (`isView`, `isModalView`,
+  `isOpenModalServerInteraction`, …). Nothing in the monorepo calls them.
+
+`apps/meteor` also depends on a patched `typia@9.7.2`, only because the built `ui-kit` requires `typia` at runtime.
+
+## Problem
+
+- **Toolchain lock.** Both packages build through `ttsc` with the typia transform plugin, and keep TypeScript 5.9 for
+  their editor and `typecheck` path. They are the packages listed as blocked in
+  [typescript-7-migration.md](../typescript-7-migration.md).
+- **Post-processing that must follow typia.** `Ajv.ts` carries `normalizeForAjv2020`, about 70 lines that rewrite
+  typia's output into what `ajv/dist/2020` accepts: it reopens closed objects, turns nullable `oneOf`s into type
+  arrays, rewrites `additionalItems` and drops `discriminator.mapping`. The 9.x → 13 upgrade changed that output and
+  400-ed REST responses in `TEST_MODE` until the normalizer caught up. Every typia upgrade carries that risk.
+- **A patch to maintain.** `.yarn/patches/typia-npm-9.7.2-*.patch` fixes the ESM default export for Meteor.
+- **Two schema systems.** `core-typings` already depends on Zod (`~4.3.6`). `IBanner`, `IRocketChatRecord` and the
+  `cloud/*` payloads are Zod-first (`interface X extends z.infer<typeof XSchema>`), and the apps converters use Zod
+  codecs ([apps-converters-zod](apps-converters-zod/README.md)). Those Zod-first types still feed typia through the
+  inferred type, so the same shape is described twice.
+
+## What Zod gives us
+
+`z.toJSONSchema(schema, { io: 'input', target: 'draft-2020-12' })` emits the dialect our Ajv instance uses. A test
+run over `IBannerSchema` showed:
+
+- Objects come out open, with no `additionalProperties: false`, which is what the REST response schemas need when
+  they combine a component `$ref` with `success` through `allOf`. That part of the normalizer goes away.
+- `TimestampSchema` (an ISO string ↔ `Date` codec) emits `type: string, format: date-time`, the same as typia. The
+  pattern also requires the `Z` suffix, which `Date.prototype.toISOString` always produces.
+- Only the build changes. Zod schemas are plain runtime values, so `core-typings` and `ui-kit` can build with `tsgo`
+  and drop `ttsc`.
+
+## The trap: `z.custom`
+
+`IBan

pr_events.title: feat: show the web client commit next to the server commit in Workspace
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Proposed changes

When the web client is served from another host than the server (`ui-preview`, or `yarn dev` with `RC_SERVER_URL`), Administration > Workspace > Deployment only shows the server's commit, so there is no way to tell which client build is running.

The client already knows its own commit: the Vite build writes it into `rocketchat.info`. The Deployment card now compares it with the server's and, when they differ, shows a **Web client commit details** row with the client's HEAD and branch. When the server serves its own client both commits match and the card is unchanged.

Preview builds of pull requests check out the detached merge ref, so `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns `HEAD`; the build now takes the branch from `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` when it is set.

pr_events.title: feat: skip the Site URL change prompt in the standalone client
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Proposed changes

The standalone web client (`ui-preview`, or `yarn dev` with `RC_SERVER_URL`) runs on another origin than the server's `Site_Url` by design. Admins got the "The setting Site URL is configured to … Do you want to change to …?" prompt on every load, and confirming it would point the server's `Site_Url` at the proxy.

The standalone build now swaps `useRootUrlChange` for a no-op, through the same `nativeModules` replacement that already swaps `getURL`. The client the server serves keeps the prompt.

## Issue(s)

https://rocketchat.atlassian.net/browse/ARCH-2652

Found while taking the screenshot for #43378.

## Steps to test or reproduce

1. `cd apps/meteor && RC_SERVER_URL=https://open.rocket.chat yarn dev`
2. Log in as an admin.
3. No Site URL change prompt shows. On `develop` it shows on every load.

## Further comments

Checked with Playwright against open.rocket.chat: the prompt showed before the change and no longer shows after it.

Introduced by #43329 meeting #43281 when `release-9.0.0` was merged into `develop` (d715505026).

## Proposed changes

#43329 on the release branch added a spec that mounts the API through `Router.router`; #43281 on `develop` had removed that getter. The `🔎 Code Check / TypeScript` job fails on `develop`:

```
server/api/ApiClass.refusals.spec.ts(70,38): error TS2339: Property 'router' does not exist on type 'Router<any, any, any>'.

The spec would not run either: `./api` now imports `httpServer`, which touches `WebApp` on load.

The spec now mounts its router the way the other API specs do since #43281 (`createRootApp` + `mountRouter` + `createNodeServer`), and mocks `../lib/http/httpServer` with a bare root app instead of `meteor/webapp`.

## Steps to test or reproduce

- `cd apps/meteor && yarn .testunit:jest server/api/ApiClass.refusals.spec.ts` → 13 passed
- `cd apps/meteor && yarn typecheck` → no errors

- This PR fixes #22686

cc @yi-nuo426

### Summary of Changes

1. **UUID Path Parameter Validation (`http.StatusBadRequest`)**:
   - In both `GetMeshSyncResourceByID` and `DeleteMeshSyncResource` (`server/handlers/meshsync_handler.go`), path parameter `id` is now validated via `uuid.FromString(resourceID)`.
   - Returns `models.ErrInvalidUUID(err)` with HTTP 400 Bad Request if the UUID format is invalid, immediately failing before querying the database.

2. **Accurate REST 404 Status Semantics (`http.StatusNotFound`)**:
   - In `GetMeshSyncResourceByID`: When the resource does not exist in the database, `gorm.ErrRecordNotFound` is caught via `errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound)` and mapped to `models.ErrResultNotFound(err)` with HTTP 404 Not Found rather than unconditionally returning HTTP 500 (`ErrFetchMeshSyncResources`).
   - In `DeleteMeshSyncResource`: Checks `tx.RowsAffected == 0` upon deletion. If no resource was affected/found, returns

+// isValidMeshSyncResourceID validates that a resource ID is either a valid UUID or
+// a valid base64-encoded composite identifier (such as the composite keys generated by MeshSync SetID:
+// clusterID.kind.apiVersion.namespace.name).
+func isValidMeshSyncResourceID(id string) bool {
+	id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
+	if id == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	if _, err := uuid.FromString(id); err == nil {
+		return true
+	}
+
+	var decoded string
+	if data, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(id); err == nil && len(data) > 0 {
+		decoded = string(data)
+	} else if data, err := base64.URLEncoding.DecodeString(id); err == nil && len(data) > 0 {
+		decoded = string(data)
+	} else if data, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(id); err == nil && len(data) > 0 {
+		decoded = string(data)
+	}
+
+	if decoded != "" {
+		parts := strings.Split(decoded, ".")
+		if len(parts) >= 4 {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}

pr_events.title: compose_paste: Preserve markdown link syntax when quoting spaced URLs.
pr_events.body_excerpt:
Selecting an entire rendered link with spaces in its URL, such as `[https://example.com/docs/my file.pdf](https://example.com/docs/my%20file.pdf)`, and quoting or copy-pasting that selection wraps the link inside a `

` element in the clipboard fixture (`

...

`). Because `P` is not in `outer_elements_to_retain`, the paste converter took the single-textful-child plain-text fast path and returned the bare text node value, dropping the `` element and its `href`. The unencoded spaces then prevented the compose box markdown parser from auto-linking it. Similar to how mentions are preserved when wrapped in `

`, ensure any fragment containing an `` element bypasses the plain-text fast path so it reaches Turndown's `links` rule to retain proper markdown link syntax. Fixes #40138.

pr_events.title: [mesheryctl] system start / system reset delete a "manifests" folder in the current directory
pr_events.body_excerpt:
**Notes for Reviewers**

- This PR fixes #22690

### What was wrong
Running `mesheryctl system reset` (or `system start` on Kubernetes) deleted any `manifests` folder in the directory you ran it from, including your own files, without any warning. mesheryctl was only supposed to clean out its own folder at `~/.meshery/manifests`.

### What changed
- mesheryctl now deletes only its own `~/.meshery/manifests` folder. It never touches a `manifests` folder where you run the command. This is a one-line change in `CreateManifestsFolder()`.
- Added a regression test (`TestCreateManifestsFolder`) that checks a user's `manifests` folder survives and mesheryctl's own folder is still cleaned and recreated.

### How it was tested
- The new test passes with the fix and fails without it.
- All `mesheryctl/pkg/utils` tests pass.
- Ran `mesheryctl system reset -y` from a folder containing `manifests/`. The files are no longer deleted.

pr_events.title: fix(saml): accept {{field}} placeholders from the field map example
pr_events.body_excerpt:
## Proposed changes (including videos or screenshots)

The help text for the SAML User Data Field Map shows `{{firstName}} {{lastName}}` and `{{identifier}}`, but `fillTemplateData` only replaced `__name__` placeholders. The double underscores in the source string get turned into `{{ }}` when the i18n strings are built, so anyone copying the example ended up with the literal text `{{firstName}} {{lastName}}` as their full name.

Rather than touching the translation string, `fillTemplateData` now accepts both forms, and the `{{identifier}}` key and the `{{regex}}` check are handled the same way as their `__x__` versions. Existing `__x__` configs keep working as before.

## Issue(s)

Closes #31743

## Steps to test or reproduce

1. Set the User Data Field Map to the example from the setting description, e.g. `"name": { "fieldNames": ["firstName", "lastName"], "template": "{{firstName}} {{lastName}}" }`
2. Log in through SAML
3. Before: the name is the literal template. After: it's filled
